correctness.rationale: For prime p, every orbit of an edge is a spanning p-cycle, forcing two-vertex-connectivity; for composite n an orbit at any nontrivial step divisor gives a disconnected invariant face. Hence the geometric action is free exactly for primes. The cited 1997 theorem gives (2p-6)-connectivity, so the orbit quotient is a classifying-space approximation in degrees below 2p-5, with cyclic group homology and integral periodic cohomology. The cup products follow from naturality. Standard group cohomology and LS cup-length inequality apply. Exhaustive checks for n=3..6 confirm stabilizers and Euler counts, not the general theorem.

value.rationale: The cyclic relabeling quotient is a canonical topological orbit of the Vassiliev-motivated separable-graph complex. The exact prime/composite free-action boundary is structural, not an arbitrary numerical slice. The resulting family has p-torsion in an unbounded number of lower homological degrees and nonzero powers of a natural degree-two class through p-3, forcing unbounded LS-category while its covering space remains a wedge of spheres. This multiplicative integral information is not provided by previously known rational character tables.
